metadata.title: Oracle Slides 3.4% as Buy Call Meets a Capital Burden

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Oracle (NYSE:ORCL), the database and AI-cloud heavyweight, received fresh bullish attention Friday as Barron's argued that its accelerating operating momentum could ultimately translate into stronger cash generation for shareholders. Investors were not buying the optimism yet: shares dropped approximately 3.4% to $145.45, based on Friday's price.
Executive Chairman Larry Ellison also canceled a trading plan that could have allowed him to sell as many as 50 million Oracle shares. The company said Ellison had sold none of the stock covered by the arrangement before terminating it, while providing no explanation for the decision. At $145.45 per share, the maximum authorization would have represented roughly $7.27 billion of Oracle stocklarge enough to matter for investor perception even though the transaction would have been Ellison's personal sale rather than corporate fundraising.
The cancellation takes one possible overhang off the table, but it does nothing directly for Oracle's balance sheet, AI infrastructure spending or debt load because any proceeds would have gone to Ellison. The valuation picture is more striking: the chart places Oracle's GF Value at $191.47 versus a $145.45 market price, leaving the stock 24.04% below that benchmark. That gap gives investors a clear valuation counterpoint to Friday's selloff, but closing it will ultimately depend on Oracle turning its huge AI-cloud ambitions into durable revenue growth and cash flow.
